producer_report.summary: A landed request now stops addressing a failure cause once an introspection of that cause is recorded after the landing, so recurring failures can be queued again. In `addressing_request` (hestia.rs), the landed branch makes the same check as the closed-by-person branch: the landing time must not be earlier than the newest introspection. An open request still addresses the cause. The module doc and the function doc say so, and CHANGELOG.md has a new Fixed entry. I added two unit tests, one for the landed case (before and after a recurrence) and one for the open case. The `backlog()` fixture used to land a request before its own introspections, so I moved its landing later. The hestia tests (87) and the full athena-core suite passed. The policy scan passed. I did not run clippy or the other crates' tests.
